title: Dimension multiplication at a restricted highest weight
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: it is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ with unipotent radical $U$, with these notions as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Use the character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and integer pairing of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$ as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. A rational $S$-module is an $F$-vector space $V$ with coaction $c_V:V\to V\otimes_F F[S]$ satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity. A submodule is a linear subspace stable under this coaction, and simple means nonzero with only zero and itself as submodules. Write $V^U$ for the vectors whose restricted coaction is $v\mapsto v\otimes1$. A finite-dimensional simple module has highest weight $\eta\in X$ if $V^U$ is one-dimensional and $t v=\eta(t)v$ on this line after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Write $\dim_F$ for ordinary vector-space dimension, an integer rather than its image in $F$. Assume $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$. Let $\lambda,\mu\in X$ be dominant, meaning nonnegative pairing with each simple coroot, and suppose $\lambda$ is $p$-restricted:
$$0\le\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle<p\quad(\alpha\in\Delta).$$
For any finite-dimensional simple rational $S$-modules $V_\lambda,V_\mu,V_{\lambda+p\mu}$ with respective highest weights $\lambda,\mu,\lambda+p\mu$, one has the integer identity
$$\dim_F V_{\lambda+p\mu}=(\dim_F V_\lambda)(\dim_F V_\mu).$$
This assertion does not require any chosen Frobenius endomorphism or any identification with regular-function induced modules. It includes zero weights and the trivial group.

source.place: Part II, 3.16--3.17: Steinberg tensor product theorem, numerical consequence; WANTED: this book is not local. Online corroboration read: Williamson, Algebraic representations and constructible sheaves, arXiv:1610.06261v1, section 1.4, Theorem 1.3 and equation (1.7), pp.6--7, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.06261. Frobenius twist preserves vector-space dimension.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $S$ is reductive and $X$ is the finite-rank free character lattice of its reduced root datum. The map $a:X\to X$, $x\mapsto px$, is injective with finite cokernel $X/pX$. Take the identity root correspondence and $q_\alpha=p$; its dual is also multiplication by $p$, so both required root and coroot equalities hold. Apply [lem-sfb-root-datum-isogeny-realization] with source and target $(S,T)$ to obtain a surjective homomorphism $f:S\to S$ with finite kernel and $(f|_T)^*=p\,\mathrm{id}_X$. This auxiliary choice adds no hypothesis to the assertion.

source.place: Example 23.3, printed p.484, and Theorem 23.9, printed p.487.

proof.text: The smooth $F$-scheme $S$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied to its structure morphism. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $f$, factoring it as a faithfully flat map onto a closed subgroup $I$ followed by $I\hookrightarrow S$. Surjectivity of $f$ says that this closed immersion has full support. Its defining ideal is contained in every prime of the reduced ring $F[S]$, hence is zero. Thus $I=S$ and $f$ is faithfully flat, as required for the root-power law.

source.place: Theorem 5.39, printed p.108; reducedness: Stacks Tag 056T, varieties.tex, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-isogeny-root-power-laws] to $f$. For corresponding roots $\alpha,\beta$ it gives $p\beta=e_\alpha\alpha$ with $e_\alpha>0$. Reducedness of the root system forces $\beta=\alpha$ and then $e_\alpha=p$. Thus $f$ maps each root subgroup into itself, as a scheme morphism over every test algebra. By the ordered multiplication isomorphism of [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], every element of $U(A)$ is a product of positive root subgroup elements, for every $F$-algebra $A$. Applying $f$ to that product shows $f(U)\subseteq U$ scheme-theoretically, including the empty-root case.

source.place: Proposition 23.5 and formula (146), printed pp.485--486; Theorem 21.68(a), printed p.445.

proof.text: Define $W=f^*V_\mu$ by the coaction $(1\otimes f^\#)c_{V_\mu}$ on the unchanged vector space $V_\mu$. Since $f$ is a group homomorphism, its pullback respects comultiplication and counit, so the coaction identities follow from those of $c_{V_\mu}$. Set $Q=V_\lambda\otimes_F W$ with diagonal coaction: $s(v\otimes w)=sv\otimes f(s)w$. The two group action identities follow by substitution, so this is a finite-dimensional rational module. Apply [lem-sfb-restricted-frobenius-tensor-simplicity]: the given weights are dominant, the first is $p$-restricted, both factors before pullback are simple, and steps 1--3 give all hypotheses on $f$. Hence $Q$ is simple.

source.place: Part II, 3.16--3.17; WANTED. Online corroboration read: Williamson arXiv:1610.06261v1, section 1.4, Theorem 1.3, p.6.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne v\in V_\lambda^U$ and $0\ne w\in V_\mu^U$. Their tensor is nonzero: choose linear functionals taking value $1$ on $v,w$, whose tensor takes value $1$ on $v\otimes w$. For every $F$-algebra $A$, $u\in U(A)$ fixes $v\otimes w$, because $u$ fixes $v$ and $f(u)\in U(A)$ fixes $w$. For $t\in T(A)$ its action on this tensor is $\lambda(t)\mu(f(t))=\lambda(t)\mu(t)^p=(\lambda+p\mu)(t)$. By [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight], simplicity of $Q$ implies that $Q^U$ is one-dimensional. Its nonzero vector $v\otimes w$ therefore spans it, proving that $Q$ has highest weight $\lambda+p\mu$. The uniqueness clause of the same cited node now gives an equivariant $F$-linear isomorphism $Q\simeq V_{\lambda+p\mu}$.

source.place: Theorems 22.18 and 22.19, printed pp.467--468; explicit tensor calculation written by Q54.

proof.text: If $(e_i)_{i=1}^a$ and $(h_j)_{j=1}^b$ are bases of $V_\lambda$ and $V_\mu$, then $(e_i\otimes h_j)_{i,j}$ spans $Q$ by bilinearity and is independent by applying each pair of dual coordinate functionals. Thus $\dim_F Q=ab$. The pullback has not changed the underlying vector space, and the isomorphism of step 5 preserves dimension, so $\dim_F V_{\lambda+p\mu}=(\dim_F V_\lambda)(\dim_F V_\mu)$ as integers. No scalar reduction modulo $p$ occurred. The argument also covers zero weights; for the trivial group each simple module is one-dimensional and the identity reads $1=1\cdot1$.
